title: Latency budget enforcer and regional tilt mitigation hotfix
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Hotfix: add latency-budget enforcer (probabilistic soft-shedding) and regional tilt detector to reduce cross-zone impact during asymmetric spikes. Adds telemetry for tilt incidents and a runtime flag to tune soft-shed aggressiveness.
description: Motivation: Recent incident (SUP-3021) showed tenancy-level P95 excursions in single regions causing noisy cross-region failovers. This hotfix introduces a lightweight latency-budget enforcer that applies probabilistic, low-impact shedding when a tenant's short-window budget is exceeded, and a regional tilt detector that attenuates admission from a tilted region while preserving global fairness. Goals: 1) Reduce noisy cross-region re-routing during short surges, 2) Keep impact per-tenant minimal (soft drop vs hard eviction), 3) Provide observability hooks for incident triage. Changes included: - introduce serve/shedder/latency_budget.go: sliding-window budget calculator (50ms buckets, configurable window), probabilistic soft-shedding with exponential cooldown per-tenant - introduce serve/router/tilt_detector.go: region-level tilt detector using asymmetric ingress delta and heat score, exposes tear-down signal to router - add console/telemetry/tilt_metric_exporter.go: new metrics: redwood.region.tilt_score, redwood.shed.rate_by_tenant, redwood.shed.recovery_cooldown - k8s config tweak deploy/k8s/redwood-config.yaml: runtime feature flag runtime.flags.latency_soft_shed (default=true) and tilt_sensitivity (0..1) - tests/tests/tilt_simulation_test.go: deterministic simulation harness and unit tests to validate scoring/backoff - docs/docs/ops/tilt-mitigation.md: operator runbook and suggested runbooks for threshold tuning Checklist: - [x] implement algorithm and unit tests - [x] add telemetry and dashboards (minimal) - [x] add runtime flag and config override - [x] integration test simulation - [x] manual canary in staging / smoke ok Commits (high level): - 1a2b3c4 add latency budget enforcer and tests - 2b3c4d5 add regional tilt detector and router integration - 3c4d5e6 export tilt metrics and add flags - 4d5e6f7 fix cooldown off-by-one and add more unit coverage Review summary: Initial design reviewed by Luca and Priya; Luca asked for stronger metrics around false-positive shedding and a runtime override; Priya flagged potential interaction with existing KV-preserve logic. Changes made: added shed.reason tag, exposed runtime.flags.latency_soft_shed, adjusted backoff to avoid immediate reopen oscillation (cooldown doubled). Review conversation (abridged): - Luca Romano (2026-02-19): "Good direction. Please add shed.reason tag and a counter for false positives so SRE can tune sensitivity." - Maya Patel (2026-02-19): "Added shed.reason tag and a rejected_count metric; also added an operator flag to force-disable soft-shed for emergency rollback." - Priya Singh (2026-02-20): "Check interaction with kv-preserve path: we must avoid shedding requests that carry recoverable KV state." - Maya Patel (2026-02-20): "Added explicit bypass for KV-preserve marker headers; added unit tests covering that path." - Alex Kim (2026-02-21): "Integration test failed on first run (e2e timeout). Reran and passed; left one flaky test marked with @flake label." CI and validation: - First pipeline: unit & integration passed, e2e timed out (one test). - Reran e2e after increasing test timeout and isolating flake; final CI green. Merge decision: After two approvals (Luca, Priya) and green CI, PR was squashed and merged. Post-merge actions: - Stage rollout: feature enabled by default in staging and canary, runtime flag off for top-tier customers for 48h to observe. - Telemetry: added Grafana panel redwood.region.tilt_score and alert redwood.tilt.high (threshold tuned conservatively). Observed behavior in canary: slight reduction in cross-region failovers and tenant-level P95 drop ~12% on simulated tilt workload. Operator notes: - If false positives observed, set runtime.flags.latency_soft_shed=false for the affected namespace and open ENG-4991. - Tilt sensitivity is conservative by default; for aggressive mitigation increase tilt_sensitivity to 0.6 but test in canary first.
